title: clusterSnap docstring example contradicts the code's even-length median selection
description: clusterSnap snaps each cluster to cluster[Math.floor(cluster.length / 2)], i.e. the UPPER-middle element for even-length clusters. The docstring's own worked example claims the cluster [250,253] snaps to 250, but for a 2-element cluster Math.floor(2/2) = 1, so cluster[1] = 253 is selected — the function snaps to 253, not 250. The odd-length example ([100,103,108]->103) is correct and is pinned by tests, but the even-length behavior is undocumented/misdocumented and untested. The actual code path always picks the larger of the two middle values, which is a deterministic but asymmetric 'representative', not the arithmetic median the comment implies. Functionally the snap is still consistent (all cluster members receive the same value, so visual alignment holds), so this is a comment-correctness/spec defect rather than a runtime mis-render, but a maintainer relying on the documented example would compute the wrong expected output (e.g. when adding a regression test).
evidence: Line 38: `const median = cluster[Math.floor(cluster.length / 2)]`. For cluster = [250,253]: cluster.length = 2 -> Math.floor(1) = 1 -> cluster[1] = 253. Docstring lines 25-26 assert `[250,253]→250`. No test in frontend/src/__tests__/utils/layout.test.ts or frontend/src/utils/__tests__/layout.test.ts exercises an even-length cluster, so the discrepancy is unguarded.
